mechanism: Embed the block (L_k, U_k] injectively in the CRT torus Z/Q_k (wheel faithfulness: Q_k > 6·U_k gives each block element a unique residue, and ρ_{k,n} < 1/6 is exactly the statement that the sampling window occupies a small arc). The square samples X_n = (n+1)²−1 are the orbit of a two-step Weyl skew product T on Z × Z/Q_k: increments X_{n+1}−X_n = 2n+3 form an affine cocycle, so sampling is a zero-entropy 2-step nilsystem orbit — and the pinned start L_k = W_{k-1} ≡ 0 mod every prime ≤ p_{k-1} places the orbit at the distinguished zero point of the torus. Realize the scalar face H_{k,n} = C_{k,n} − 2E_{k,n} as the Birkhoff sum along this orbit of a SINGLE observable F_k on Z/Q_k built from the kernel-checked identity (centered prime comb minus twice the Mertens-weighted reciprocal-interval discrepancies), so the C−2E correlation is preserved by construction and never split by a triangle inequality. Then solve the finite cohomological equation F_k = G_k∘T − G_k + R_k, where R_k is the projection onto the obstruction space of the finite Weyl system; the coboundary part telescopes to two boundary evaluations of the transfer function G_k, and the obstruction part's Birkhoff sums are exactly incomplete quadratic Gauss sums Σ_{r<H} e_{Q_k}(a(N+r+1)²) weighted by the Fourier coefficients c_a(F_k). Quadratic exponential sums mod Q obey square-root-in-modulus cancellation (≤ √(2·gcd(a,Q)·Q)·log Q by completion/Weyl differencing, with the complete sums at the pinned zero start being classical evaluable Gauss sums), and the packet's own numerology makes this land on target: Q_k ≍ 6·p_k·W_{k-1} ≍ p_k·X_n, so √Q_k ≪ X_n^{1/2}(log X_n)^{1/2}, inside the ε-loss. The final bound is |H_{k,n}| ≤ 2‖G_k‖_∞ + (Σ_{a≠0} |c_a(F_k)|)·√(2Q_k)·log Q_k, so the entire problem re-concentrates into two finite, computable quantities per wheel level: the sup-norm of the transfer function and the ℓ¹ Fourier mass of the combined observable. Rung 2 follows if ‖G_k‖_∞ ≪ X_n^{1/2+ε} and Σ|c_a(F_k)| ≪ X_n^ε; the Fourier coefficients are Mertens/prime character-type sums mod Q_k, which is where the arithmetic hardness reappears and where I state it plainly rather than hiding it.
new_leverage: Three things a standard application does not give. (1) The pinned primorial start is converted from liability to asset: W_{k-1} is the zero point of the CRT torus, so the obstruction Gauss sums are centered/complete-type with explicit classical evaluations — no averaging over starts is needed anywhere, and no exceptional-set removal arises. (2) The C−2E correlation is preserved exactly because the decomposition is applied to the single combined observable F_k, not to C and E separately; the cohomological equation is linear and sign-blind, so the empirically observed cancellation is carried intact into the coefficients c_a(F_k) — this is precisely the packet's requested 'exact transformation preserving the C − 2E correlation'. (3) The modulus-to-scale ratio Q_k ≍ p_k·X_n is a designed coincidence unavailable to generic setups: square-root cancellation IN THE MODULUS equals the rung-2 target IN THE VARIABLE, up to (log)^{1/2} ⊂ X^ε. Even if the angle stalls, it produces a hardness-concentration theorem: the target is reduced to a bound on one explicit finite Fourier ℓ¹ mass per wheel level, a strictly sharper open question than the original estimate.
target_estimate: Named estimate: 'Pinned wheel coboundary reduction with quadratic Gauss majorant'. Statement in the packet's variables: for every k and every window (N, H) with H ≤ N and samples X_{N+r} in the synchronized block, |H_{k,N}| ≤ 2‖G_k‖_∞ + M_k·√(2Q_k)·(log Q_k), where G_k solves F_k = G_k∘T − G_k + R_k on Z/Q_k along the quadratic sampling orbit and M_k := Σ_{a≠0}|c_a(F_k)| is the nonzero-mode Fourier ℓ¹ mass of the combined centered observable (zero mode already eliminated exactly by the kernel-checked contraction). The Gauss-sum ingredient I would prove unconditionally: |Σ_{r<H} e_{Q_k}(a(N+r+1)²)| ≤ √(2·gcd(a,Q_k)·Q_k)·log Q_k uniformly in the pinned N, with gcd-losses summable because Q_k is p_k-smooth. Loss accounting: √Q_k ≪ √(6·p_k)·X_n^{1/2}, a (log X)^{1/2} factor absorbed by ε; boundary terms cost 2‖G_k‖_∞. Rung 2 (X^{1/2+ε} scalar face, hence C·H·N^{2+ε} for the Gram form since X_n ≍ N²) follows if and only if additionally ‖G_k‖_∞ ≪_ε X_n^{1/2+ε} and M_k ≪_ε X_n^ε — the two quantities the reduction isolates.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Addressed head-on and used as an asset: the orbit starts at the torus zero point (W_{k-1} ≡ 0 mod all p ≤ p_{k-1}), making the obstruction sums complete/centered Gauss sums with explicit evaluations. No L²-averaging over translates appears; every bound is pointwise in the pinned start. This is the one obstacle the angle genuinely dissolves rather than sidesteps.
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: Concur there is no family; the angle needs none. Family-averaging is replaced by single-modulus complete-sum cancellation (Gauss sums), which is a pointwise phenomenon. Off-diagonal Gram pairs map to differences X_{n+r} − X_{n'} — again quadratic polynomials — handled by the same exponential sums mod Q_k, with multiplicity exactly 1 by wheel faithfulness (Q_k > 6·U_k means distinct block elements never collide in a residue).
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Concur. Nothing here averages over moduli or residue classes; the reciprocal-d family enters only inside the construction of the single observable F_k and is never disassembled. The modulus Q_k is fixed per level, not varied.
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: Avoided in form: M(d) weights stay signed inside the Fourier coefficients c_a(F_k); no |M(d)| ≤ Kd^{1/2+ε} insertion occurs and no operator norm with absolute values is formed. Residual risk stated honestly: if bounding M_k = Σ|c_a| can only be done by taking absolute values of the M(d)-weighted contributions coefficientwise, the same overloaded operator returns through the back door. The angle succeeds only if the cohomological step redistributes the signs into oscillating coefficient sums — this is checkable, see kill test.
obstacle_positions.parity: Not sieve-only: the quadratic phases e_{Q}(a n²) are analytic Type-I-and-a-half input beyond any sieve axiom system, so the parity barrier does not categorically block the skeleton. However, the coefficients c_a(F_k) are prime/Mertens sums twisted by characters mod Q_k, and evaluating those to square-root accuracy unconditionally is exactly the parity/GRH wall relocated. My position: parity does not kill the reduction, but it very likely blocks the final coefficient bound unconditionally; I do not claim to cross it.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: The kill test below is exact finite linear algebra per wheel level (coboundary residual computation), not exponent-fitting across dyadic scales; growth of ‖G_k‖_∞ and M_k across k = 2..6 is measured against the exact predicted scales, and numerics are used only for falsification, never as evidence of truth.

kill_test: For k = 2..5 (Q_k up to ~10^4–10^5, trivial dense linear algebra): construct F_k explicitly on Z/Q_k from the kernel-checked C − 2E identity, solve the finite cohomological equation along the quadratic sampling orbit (a circulant-type linear system in the orbit coordinates), and compute exactly (i) ‖G_k‖_∞ / √X and (ii) M_k = Σ_{a≠0}|c_a(F_k)| together with M_k·√Q_k / √X. If either ratio grows like a positive power of X across these four levels — in particular if the Fourier mass M_k behaves like the absolute-value-inserted operator of obstacle 4 (i.e., ≫ X^δ for some δ > 0) — the angle is dead at rung 2 and the result is only the reduction theorem. This costs hours, not weeks, and is decisive because both quantities are exact finite objects, not asymptotic estimates.
rung0_plan: Same skeleton, weaker ingredient: replace Gauss-sum square-root cancellation by (a) Weyl equidistribution of the quadratic orbit on Z/Q_k and (b) Davenport–Vinogradov type bounds Σ_{n≤N} μ(n)e(nα) ≪_A N/(log N)^A and its Λ-analogue for rational α with smooth denominator — unconditional, classical, and exactly the quantitative shadow of Möbius disjointness from the 2-step nilsystem (this is the Sarnak-program content of the angle: the sampling system has zero entropy, so orthogonality at o(x) is forced). The coefficient sums c_a(F_k) then need only log-power savings, which Siegel–Walfisz-strength inputs supply since Q_k is p_k-smooth (no Siegel-zero anxiety for smooth moduli at fixed level: the characters mod Q_k factor through small prime-power conductors). Output: |H_{k,n}| ≪_A X_n/(log X_n)^A uniformly in the pinned start — a genuine rung-0 closure of the identical machinery, which is the angle's viability certificate.
plausible_partial: Realistically provable at bounded effort: (1) the full reduction theorem — target estimate ⟺ {‖G_k‖_∞ ≪ X^{1/2+ε} and M_k ≪ X^ε} — with the Gauss-majorant lemma proved unconditionally; this is a hardness-concentration result that converts the open estimate into two explicit finite quantities per wheel level. (2) The rung-0 statement |H_{k,n}| ≪_A X/(log X)^A unconditionally via Davenport-type twisted sums over the smooth modulus, uniform in the pinned primorial start. (3) The k = 2..5 exact coboundary diagnostic (the kill test) as a computational deliverable settling whether the Fourier mass M_k is ε-small in practice. I do not claim rung 1 or rung 2 unconditionally; rung 1 becomes plausible only if the diagnostic reveals M_k bounded by a fixed power X^{θ−1/2} with θ < 1, in which case the same pipeline gives that θ.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely to be false, stated plainly: that the Fourier ℓ¹ mass M_k = Σ_{a≠0}|c_a(F_k)| of the combined Mertens-weighted observable is X^ε-small. The coefficients are prime- and μ-sums twisted by characters mod Q_k, and for the real characters among them a square-root-accurate bound is GRH-hard; the cohomological transformation may therefore be an exact repackaging of the original difficulty rather than a reduction of it — the angle's floor is the reduction theorem plus rung 0, not a path to rung 2. Secondary risk: ‖G_k‖_∞ can blow up when the quadratic orbit has small spectral gaps against low-order characters (small denominators in the cohomological equation), and the pinned start, while symmetric, does not by itself control the transfer-function norm.
